title: Infra shift pocket notes
content:
Quick pocket notes for midday shift — mostly for me. Keep terse.

Context:
- Today: unexpected preemption on gpu-pool-03 around 08:42 — several short-lived evictions, likely host noisy-neighbor. Need to track if it's kernel-level or rfuzz driver.
- Capacity target this week: buffer 15% spare GPUs for burst backend tests. Current reserved: 420 GPUs, target headroom: 63 GPUs.

Morning checklist (walk the list):
- [ ] Confirm remaining preemptible queue drained (kubectl get pods -n gpu-preempt | grep Pending)
- [x] Bumped autoscaler min from 380 -> 400 for warm pool (temp)
- [ ] Verify NTP drift on rack-7 boxes (ntpstat / timedatectl)
- [ ] Re-run small stress job on pool-05 to reproduce eviction pattern (stress-ng -c 1 -t 60s)

Quick commands I keep forgetting:
- Show GPU pods with node: kubectl get pods -n gpu -o wide --selector=pool=dedicated
- Node GPU health: ssh infra@node-88 "nvidia-smi --query-gpu=temperature.gpu,utilization.gpu --format=csv,noheader"
- Drain node but keep pods schedulable: kubectl cordon node-XX && kubectl drain node-XX --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --disable-eviction

Networking / routing reminders:
- When perf spikes correlate with 10.1.42.x flaps — check ToR switch 7B logs, ACL change window 02:00–03:00 could've overlapped.
- If pings to model-store timeout, restart envoy on edge-proxy-2: sudo systemctl restart envoy

Observed anomalies / notes to triage:
- model-store S3 proxy returned 503 for ~40s at 07:58; suspect transient rate limiting from cloud gateway. Ticketed to cloud-net (JIRA-OPS-324).
- GPU temps trending +6C above baseline on node-12 after thermal-paste swap last month — monitor next 48h.

Handoff bullet points for next shift:
- Keep an eye on pool-03 eviction logs: /var/log/kubelet/eviction.log -> grep for OOM/killed-by-driver
- If preemptible backlog > 20, escalate to oncall infra (pager duty: infra-oncall).
- Manual fallback: spin up 4x small-quantized instances (model-quant-small) in region-us-west-2 until pool stabilizes.

Follow-ups (short):
- Ask infra-release for kernel roll-forward notes (PR#842) — could fix driver race.
- Add alert: node_gpu_temp_delta > 5C for 10m -> page SRE.
- Draft short runbook for preemption pattern (start with this doc + logs).

Sticky questions / to-do later:
- Is there an automated test we can run to reproduce noisy-neighbor? (simulate network saturation + CPU steal)
- How to get better signal for nvlink errors across racks? add nv_peer_mem counters to metrics?

Random notes to self:
- Check stash: /mnt/ops/hand-offs/ashas-notes-2025-11 (old) -> copy any useful commands into templates.
- Today felt busy — log exact incident times to make SLA postmortem easier.

Snippets for runbook (paste-ready):
1) Grab eviction events: journalctl -u kubelet --since "2h" | grep Eviction
2) Quick reschedule: kubectl scale deployment/model-worker --replicas=0 -n models && sleep 10 && kubectl scale deployment/model-worker --replicas=6 -n models
3) Reclaim GPU from preemptible: python tools/reclaim_gpus.py --pool pool-03 --count 4

End quick notes.

Notes-to-self: keep this short; transfer to confluence if we need a permanent runbook.

-- Asha
